sd.claim: Weights match {{citation}} to {{decimals}} decimals, and standard deviations once the paper's population SD is converted.

methodHint.critic: Objective weights from how much each criterion varies and how much it disagrees with the others.
methodHint.entropy: Objective weights from how unevenly each criterion's values are spread over the alternatives.
methodHint.equal: Every criterion gets the same weight.
methodHint.manual: Enter your own weights. They must be 0 or more and sum to 1.
methodHint.sd: Objective weights from how widely each criterion's values spread over the alternatives.
methodHint.merec: Objective weights from how much the alternatives' overall performance drops when each criterion is removed. Every value must be above 0.

weights.normalizeHint: Divides each weight by the total, so the weights sum to 1.
weights.sumError: Weights sum to {{value}}, they must sum to 1.

methodHint.topsis: Ranks the alternatives by their distance from an ideal and a negative-ideal solution.
methodHint.saw: Weights the rescaled values of each criterion and adds them up.
methodHint.vikor: Looks for a compromise between the best total (S) and the smallest worst regret (R); a lower Q is better.
methodHint.edas: Scores each alternative by how far it lies above and below the average of all alternatives; a higher AS is better.
methodHint.waspas: Blends a weighted sum with a weighted product, which punishes a very weak value harder; a higher Q is better.
methodHint.copras: Adds up each alternative's weighted share of the benefit criteria plus a bonus that grows as its cost share shrinks; a higher Q is better.
methodHint.marcos: Measures each weighted total against an imaginary ideal and anti-ideal row; a higher f(K) is better, in the same order as SAW (Linear).
methodHint.cocoso: Reads a weighted sum S and a power sum P three ways and combines them; a higher k is better. Zeros and negative values are allowed.
methodHint.mabac: Adds up how far each alternative lies above or below a border, the geometric mean of every criterion; a higher S is better, in the same order as a min-max weighted sum. Zeros and negative values are allowed.

topsis.title: Distances to A+ and A−
topsis.caption: Closer to A+ and farther from A− gives a higher C.
topsis.projectionNote: Drawn on the two heaviest criteria; D and C use all criteria.
topsis.planeCaption: Top left is best. C is the same along each ray.

steps.s1: Each alternative is a point: its weighted normalized values on two criteria.
steps.s2: The ideal A+ takes the best value of each criterion, the anti-ideal A− the worst.
steps.s3: D+ and D− are the selected alternative's distances to the ideal and the anti-ideal.
steps.s4: Place each alternative at (D+, D−): its two distances become its coordinates.
steps.s5: Relative closeness C = D− / (D+ + D−) is the same along each ray; top left is best.

steps.s1: Contrast: σ, the standard deviation of each criterion's normalized values.
steps.s2: Conflict: Σ(1 − ρ) is large when a criterion correlates weakly or negatively with the others.
steps.s3: Information content C = σ × Σ(1 − ρ): a criterion that varies and disagrees carries more.
steps.s4: Weight w = C / ΣC: the same bars divided by the total, so the weights add up to 1.

entropy.title: Uneven shares, more weight
entropy.caption: Each bar is one alternative's share of the column total.

steps.s1: Shares: each bar is one alternative's share of the column. The dashed line is an even split.
steps.s2: Entropy e: the more even the shares, the closer e is to 1.
steps.s3: 1 − e is the information an even column lacks; the uneven criterion has more of it.
steps.s4: Weight w: 1 − e divided by the total over all criteria.

saw.title: Every part of the score has a criterion
saw.caption: Each segment is one criterion's weight times its normalized value; the bar ends at S.

steps.s1: Rescale: every value goes onto one 0 to 1 scale (r), so criteria can be added.
steps.s2: Weight: each part is multiplied by its criterion's weight; important criteria take more of the bar.
steps.s3: Add up: the bar ends at the score S, and the longest bar ranks first.

vikor.title: Group utility or the largest regret: v sets the balance
vikor.caption: Below the dashed line Q stays within DQ of the leader; without an acceptable advantage those alternatives form the compromise set.

edas.title: Better or worse than the average, criterion by criterion
edas.caption: Right of the line: weighted distance above the average; left: below it; AS divides each by the largest SP or SN.

steps.s1: Distance: right of the line is above the average, left is below it (PDA and NDA).
steps.s2: Weight: each distance is multiplied by its criterion's weight; the stacks end at SP and SN.
steps.s3: Appraisal: AS joins SP and SN in one score; the highest AS ranks first.

sd.title: Wider spread, more weight
sd.caption: Each dot is one alternative on the 0 to 1 scale; the ruler under the dots is σ.

merec.title: Remove a criterion, see how much the scores drop
merec.caption: Each segment is one alternative's drop in overall performance when the criterion is removed; together they make E.

waspas.title: Sum or product: λ sets the blend
waspas.caption: Each line is one alternative; where two lines cross, they swap places. The vertical line marks λ = 0.5.

copras.title: Benefit share plus a bonus for low cost
copras.caption: Each bar is S+ (benefit share) plus the cost bonus, which grows as the cost share S- shrinks; it ends at Q, then N in percent of the best.

steps.s1: Benefit share S+: each bar is the alternative's share of the benefit criteria.
steps.s2: Cost bonus: the smaller the cost share S− (printed), the longer the bonus.
steps.s3: Q = S+ plus the bonus; the longest bar ranks first.
steps.s4: N: each Q as a percent of the best Q.

marcos.title: Two imaginary rows to measure against
marcos.caption: The dashed rows are imaginary: the best and the worst value of every criterion. K- is a bar against the anti-ideal, K+ against the ideal; f(K) on the right.
marcos.sawCaption: Every dot lies on one line through 0, so no two alternatives can swap places.

cocoso.title: Two scores, three readings
cocoso.caption: ka is the share of the total, kb the size against the weakest provider, kc a λ-mix against the best; k combines the three.
cocoso.lambdaCaption: λ moves only kc, so the lines barely bend: here no two providers swap at any λ.

mabac.title: One border per criterion
mabac.caption: The line in every row is the border G, the geometric mean of the forklifts. Upper area: above it, lower area: below; S adds the sticks up.
mabac.sumTitle: Same order as a min-max weighted sum
mabac.sumCaption: Every dot sits on one line, so no two forklifts can swap; G only decides the sign of S.

critic.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
critic.sigma: Contrast: the sample standard deviation of each normalized column.
critic.correlation: Conflict between criteria: the Pearson correlation of every pair of normalized columns.
critic.conflict: Total conflict of each criterion: the sum of 1 minus its correlation with every criterion.
critic.information: Information content of each criterion: its standard deviation times its total conflict.
critic.informationTotal: Total information content over all criteria.
critic.weights: Weights: each criterion's share of the total information content.

entropy.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
entropy.proportionsSum: Shares: each raw value divided by its column's total. Criterion types are not used.
entropy.proportionsMinmax: Shares: each normalized value divided by its column's total.
entropy.entropy: Entropy of each criterion: 1 when the shares are equal, lower the more uneven they are.
entropy.diversification: Degree of diversification: 1 minus the entropy, the information a criterion carries.
entropy.weights: Entropy weights: each criterion's share of the total diversification.

topsis.normalized: Vector normalization: each value divided by the length of its column.
topsis.weighted: Weighted normalized matrix: each column multiplied by its weight.
topsis.idealBest: Ideal solution A+: the best weighted value on each criterion (the maximum for benefit, the minimum for cost).
topsis.idealWorst: Anti-ideal solution A-: the worst weighted value on each criterion.
topsis.distanceBest: Euclidean distance D+ of each alternative from the ideal solution.
topsis.distanceWorst: Euclidean distance D- of each alternative from the anti-ideal solution.
topsis.closeness: Closeness coefficient C = D- / (D+ + D-). A higher value ranks higher.

equal.weights: Equal weights: every criterion gets 1 / n.

saw.normalizedLinearMax: Linear max normalization: each value divided by the column maximum, or for a cost criterion the column minimum divided by the value, so the best value is 1.
saw.normalizedSum: Sum normalization: each value divided by its column total; a cost criterion uses 1 / x first, so the shares add up to 1.
saw.weighted: Contributions: each normalized value multiplied by its criterion weight.
saw.scores: Score S: the sum of an alternative's contributions. A higher value ranks higher.

vikor.best: Best value f* of each criterion: the maximum for a benefit, the minimum for a cost.
vikor.worst: Worst value f− of each criterion: the other end of its column.
vikor.weightedDistance: Weighted distance d to the best value: 0 at the best, the criterion weight at the worst.
vikor.groupUtility: Group utility S: the sum of an alternative's distances. A lower value is better.
vikor.individualRegret: Individual regret R: an alternative's largest single distance. A lower value is better.
vikor.q: Compromise index Q: S and R rescaled to 0 to 1 and mixed by v. A lower value ranks higher.
vikor.threshold: Advantage threshold DQ = 1 / (m - 1): the Q gap the first alternative needs over the second.

edas.average: Average solution AV: the mean of each criterion over all alternatives.
edas.pda: Positive distance PDA: how much better than the average an alternative is, as a share of the average.
edas.nda: Negative distance NDA: how much worse than the average an alternative is, as a share of the average.
edas.weightedPda: Weighted positive distances w PDA: what each criterion adds to SP.
edas.weightedNda: Weighted negative distances w NDA: what each criterion adds to SN.
edas.sp: SP: the sum of an alternative's weighted positive distances.
edas.sn: SN: the sum of an alternative's weighted negative distances.
edas.nsp: NSP = SP / max SP: 1 for the alternative furthest above the average.
edas.nsn: NSN = 1 - SN / max SN: 0 for the alternative furthest below the average.
edas.scores: Appraisal score AS = (NSP + NSN) / 2. A higher value ranks higher.

sd.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
sd.sigma: Spread: the sample standard deviation of each normalized column.
sd.weights: Weights: each criterion's share of the total spread.

merec.normalized: Normalization to smaller is better: benefit min / x, cost x / max, so the worst value of each column is 1 and the best the smallest.
merec.absLog: Absolute logarithm of each normalized value: 0 for the worst value, larger the better the value.
merec.performance: Overall performance of each alternative: ln(1 + the mean of its absolute logarithms over all criteria).
merec.performanceRemoved: Performance with one criterion removed: the same sum without that criterion, still divided by the number of criteria.
merec.removalEffect: Removal effect: the total drop in performance over all alternatives when the criterion is removed.
merec.weights: MEREC weights: each criterion's share of the total removal effect.

waspas.normalized: Linear max normalization: each value divided by the column maximum, or for a cost criterion the column minimum divided by the value, so the best value is 1.
waspas.wsm: Weighted sum Q1: each normalized value times its criterion weight, added up.
waspas.wpm: Weighted product Q2: each normalized value raised to its criterion weight, multiplied together. It is never above Q1.
waspas.scores: Score Q = λ Q1 + (1 - λ) Q2. A higher value ranks higher.
waspas.lambdaSweep: Q at λ = 0, 0.1, ..., 1: where two alternatives swap places as λ moves.

copras.normalizedSum: Shares r: each value divided by its column total, for benefit and cost criteria alike.
copras.weighted: Weighted shares d = w r: each column now adds up to its criterion weight.
copras.sPlus: Benefit sum S+: the weighted shares of the benefit criteria, added up.
copras.sMinus: Cost sum S-: the weighted shares of the cost criteria, added up; a smaller S- is better.
copras.significance: Relative significance Q = S+ plus the cost weight shared out in proportion to 1 / S-; a higher value ranks higher and the Q values add up to 1.
copras.utility: Utility degree N: Q as a percentage of the largest Q, so the best alternative has 100.

marcos.normalized: Normalized values n: each value against the ideal row AI (the column best), so the ideal gets 1; the same as SAW (Linear).
marcos.weighted: Weighted values v = w n: each normalized value times its criterion weight.
marcos.sAai: S_aai: the weighted total of the anti-ideal row AAI, the worst value of every criterion.
marcos.sAi: S_ai: the weighted total of the ideal row AI, which is the sum of the weights, 1.
marcos.s: Weighted total S of each alternative: the row sum of v, the same number as the SAW (Linear) score.
marcos.kMinus: Utility degree K- = S / S_aai: how many anti-ideals the alternative is worth.
marcos.kPlus: Utility degree K+ = S / S_ai: the share of the ideal the alternative reaches.
marcos.fKMinus: f(K-) = K+ / (K+ + K-): the same number for every alternative, so it is shown once.
marcos.fKPlus: f(K+) = K- / (K+ + K-): the same number for every alternative, so it is shown once.
marcos.utility: Utility f(K): K+ and K- merged by the two utility functions. A higher value ranks higher; since f(K) = c · S, the order is the order of S.

cocoso.normalized: Min-max normalization: the worst value of each column becomes 0 and the best 1, for a cost criterion the other way round. Negative values work too.
cocoso.s: Weighted sum S: each normalized value times its criterion weight, added up.
cocoso.p: Power sum P: each normalized value raised to its criterion weight, added up. A criterion with weight 0 is left out, since 0 to the power 0 would add 1 to every P.
cocoso.ka: ka: the share of S + P in the total over all alternatives.
cocoso.kb: kb: S and P each divided by the smallest one, added. It is at least 2; exactly 2 for an alternative with both the smallest S and the smallest P.
cocoso.kc: kc = (λ S + (1 - λ) P) / (λ max S + (1 - λ) max P). The best mix gets 1.
cocoso.scores: Combined score k = (ka kb kc)^(1/3) + (ka + kb + kc) / 3. A higher value ranks higher.
cocoso.lambdaSweep: k at λ = 0, 0.1, ..., 1: where two alternatives swap places as λ moves.

mabac.normalized: Min-max normalization: the worst value of each column becomes 0 and the best 1, for a cost criterion the other way round. Negative and zero values are fine too.
mabac.weighted: Weighted matrix V: each normalized value plus 1, times its criterion weight, so it lies between w and 2w.
mabac.border: Border G: the geometric mean of each column of V, computed through logarithms so that hundreds of alternatives do not underflow to 0.
mabac.distance: Distance Q = V - G: positive in the upper area (towards the best value), negative in the lower area.
mabac.scores: Distance to border S: the row sum of Q. A higher value ranks higher; S is the min-max weighted sum minus one constant, so the order is that sum's.

codes.alternatives-count-mismatch: The number of alternative names does not match the number of rows.
codes.value-out-of-range: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is too large or too small to compute with. Rescale {{criterion}} (another unit) so its values lie between 10⁻¹⁰⁰ and 10¹⁰⁰.
codes.constant-column: Every alternative has the same value on {{criterion}}, so it cannot tell them apart.
codes.non-positive-value: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is {{value}}. This method divides by the values or takes their logarithm, so each must be above 0.
codes.negative-value: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is {{value}}. Raw data (sum) needs values of 0 or more; choose Min-max to use negative values.
codes.invalid-weight: Enter a number for the weight of {{criterion}}.
codes.negative-weight: The weight of {{criterion}} is {{value}}. Weights cannot be negative.
codes.weights-sum: Weights sum to {{value}}, they must sum to 1.
codes.non-positive-average: The average of {{criterion}} is {{value}}. EDAS divides by each criterion's average, so it must be above 0.
codes.all-worst-alternative: {{alternative}} is the worst on every weighted criterion, so its S and P are 0 and CoCoSo would divide by 0. Remove it or choose another method.

critic.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its CRITIC weight is 0.
critic.few-alternatives: With fewer than 4 alternatives the correlations are unstable. Read the CRITIC weights with care.
critic.no-conflict-equal-weights: The criteria that vary carry no conflict with each other (only one varies, or they move together), so they share the weight equally.
critic.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so there is no information to weigh. Equal weights are used instead.
critic.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.

entropy.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its Entropy weight is 0.
entropy.zeros-in-column: {{criterion}} contains zeros, which can inflate its weight.
entropy.two-alternatives-minmax: With 2 alternatives, min-max gives every criterion that is not constant the same weight.
entropy.dominant-weight: {{criterion}} takes more than half of the weight, so check whether its spread is real.
entropy.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.

topsis.zero-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is 0, so it does not affect the ranking.
topsis.zero-distance: Some alternatives coincide with both the ideal and the anti-ideal solution. They get a closeness of 0.5.

vikor.constant-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is the same, so it adds nothing to S or R.
vikor.equal-group-utility: Every alternative has the same S, so Q comes from R alone and reaches at most 1 − v, which can make C1 harder to meet.
vikor.equal-regret: Every alternative has the same R, so Q comes from S alone and reaches at most v, which can make C1 harder to meet.
vikor.no-spread: Every alternative has the same S and the same R, so all get Q = 0.
vikor.tie-for-first: More than one alternative has the lowest Q; they are listed in input order and all are in the compromise set.

edas.constant-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is the same, so it adds nothing to SP or SN.
edas.negative-values: {{criterion}} has negative values. EDAS measures distance as a share of the average, so the result depends on where zero is.
edas.small-average: The average of {{criterion}} is close to 0 next to its values, so its distances grow very large and it can decide the ranking even with a small weight.
edas.no-spread: No alternative is above or below the average on a weighted criterion, so every alternative gets AS = 0.5.

sd.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its SD weight is 0.
sd.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.
sd.two-alternatives: With 2 alternatives, every criterion that is not constant gets the same SD weight.
sd.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.

merec.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so removing it changes nothing and its MEREC weight is 0.
merec.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.
merec.dominant-weight: {{criterion}} takes more than half of the weight, so check that its range is real.
merec.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet MEREC gives it a removal effect. Check whether the difference is real.

copras.no-cost-criteria: There is no cost criterion with a weight above 0, so Q = S+ and COPRAS gives the same result as SAW with the sum option.

cocoso.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.

mabac.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.
